# System for Cutting a Carcass

The system for cutting a carcass is designed to process different regions of the carcass in a controlled and sequential manner. At its core, the system includes a support assembly that is configured to move along two distinct routes: a first path and a second path. Each of these paths runs adjacent to a different portion of the carcass, allowing the system to address separate areas as the support assembly advances through its range of motion.

Integrated with the support assembly is a retractable assembly that transitions between two operating configurations depending on which path is being traversed. When the support assembly travels along the first path, the retractable assembly is placed in an extended configuration, positioning it appropriately for engagement with the carcass. Conversely, as the support assembly moves along the second path, the retractable assembly shifts into a retracted configuration, drawing away from the carcass so that it does not interfere with operations occurring along that portion of the travel.

The system employs two separate cutting tools, each dedicated to a specific portion of the carcass. The first cutting tool processes the first portion of the carcass as the support assembly moves along the first path. When the retractable assembly retracts—coinciding with the transition to the second path—the first cutting tool disengages, ceasing its interaction with the carcass. The second cutting tool then takes over, processing the second portion of the carcass while the support assembly travels along the second path.

A notable feature of the system is the independence of the two cutting tools. The first cutting tool is movable independently and separately from the movement of the second cutting tool. This independent operation allows each tool to be positioned, actuated, and controlled without being constrained by the motion of the other, providing greater flexibility and precision in processing the distinct portions of the carcass.

# System and Method for Cutting a Carcass

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to systems and methods for processing animal carcasses, and more particularly to an apparatus employing a movable support assembly and independently operable cutting tools for the precise and adaptable processing of different portions of a carcass during a cutting operation.

## Background

In conventional carcass processing operations, the ability to accurately and efficiently cut different portions of a carcass presents significant challenges. Variations in carcass size, shape, and anatomy require processing equipment capable of adjusting to differing conditions. Existing systems often rely on fixed or rigidly linked cutting mechanisms that limit the precision and adaptability of the cutting operation, resulting in inconsistent yields and reduced efficiency. There remains a need for a system that permits more flexible and accurate processing of distinct carcass portions.

## Summary of the Invention

The present system and method provide an improved approach to cutting a carcass through the use of a movable support assembly working in conjunction with two independently operable cutting tools. This configuration enables the precise processing of different portions of a carcass and offers a degree of adaptability not achieved by prior arrangements.

## Detailed Description

### The Movable Support Assembly

At the core of the system is a movable support assembly that carries and positions a retractable assembly. This support assembly is capable of traveling along two distinct paths, allowing it to guide the carcass, or the associated cutting mechanisms, relative to the portions being processed. The movement of the support along these separate paths ensures that different regions of the carcass can be brought into alignment with the appropriate cutting tools in sequence or as required by the processing task.

### The Retractable Assembly

Mounted in association with the movable support is a retractable assembly configured to transition between an extended configuration and a retracted configuration. In the extended configuration, the assembly is positioned to engage with the carcass or to facilitate the cutting operation. In the retracted configuration, the assembly withdraws, providing clearance and enabling the support to reposition without interference. This transition between configurations contributes to the overall flexibility of the system, allowing the apparatus to accommodate variations in carcass geometry and to move safely between successive cutting stages.

### The Cutting Tools

The system incorporates two independently operable cutting tools. Each cutting tool is dedicated to processing a different portion of the carcass, and each operates as the support assembly moves along its respective path. Because the tools are independently operable, they may be actuated separately, at different times, or in coordination, depending on the requirements of the particular processing operation.

### Independent Movement of the First Cutting Tool

A key innovation of the present invention resides in the capability of the first cutting tool to move separately and independently from the second cutting tool. Rather than being mechanically constrained to move in unison with the second tool, the first cutting tool possesses its own freedom of movement. This independence allows each tool to be positioned and actuated according to the specific characteristics of the carcass portion it is intended to process.

By decoupling the movement of the first cutting tool from that of the second, the system achieves more precise and adaptable processing of different carcass portions during the cutting operation. The independent movement permits fine adjustments to accommodate anatomical variations, improves cutting accuracy, and enhances the overall yield and quality of the processed product.

## Method of Operation

In operation, a carcass is presented to the system and supported relative to the movable support assembly. The support assembly travels along a first path, during which the first cutting tool—operating independently—processes a first portion of the carcass. The retractable assembly may transition between its extended and retracted configurations as needed to facilitate engagement or to provide clearance during repositioning. The support assembly subsequently travels along a second path, during which the second cutting tool processes a second portion of the carcass.

Throughout the operation, the independent movement of the first cutting tool relative to the second enables each cut to be executed with a high degree of precision, adapting to the particular contours and requirements of the respective carcass portions.

## Advantages

The disclosed system and method offer several advantages over conventional carcass processing equipment, including:

- **Increased precision** through the independent movement and actuation of the cutting tools;
- **Enhanced adaptability** to variations in carcass size and shape by virtue of the retractable assembly and separately movable tools;
- **Improved efficiency** through the coordinated yet independent processing of distinct carcass portions along two separate paths; and
- **Greater flexibility** in accommodating diverse processing tasks without requiring rigidly linked cutting mechanisms.

Together, these features provide a robust and versatile solution for the accurate and efficient cutting of carcasses.

# Patent Abstract

**Automated Carcass Cutting System**

An automated carcass cutting system for processing animal carcasses with improved precision and efficiency. The system comprises a movable support assembly configured to receive and secure a carcass in a predetermined orientation, wherein the movable support assembly is adapted to translate the carcass along a processing path. A retractable assembly is mounted proximate the processing path and is selectively deployable between an extended operative position and a retracted position, enabling controlled engagement with the carcass during cutting operations while permitting clearance during carcass loading and repositioning.

The system further includes a first cutting tool and a second cutting tool, each independently controlled by a control system to perform distinct cutting operations along different regions of the carcass. The independent control of the first and second cutting tools permits simultaneous or sequential cutting along separate cut paths, thereby increasing throughput and enabling adaptive cutting profiles based on carcass dimensions and characteristics.

In operation, the control system coordinates movement of the movable support assembly, deployment of the retractable assembly, and actuation of the first and second cutting tools to execute a predetermined cutting sequence. The system may include one or more sensors to detect carcass position, size, or anatomical features, wherein the control system adjusts the cutting operations of the first and second cutting tools in response to sensor data. The disclosed system reduces manual labor, improves cut consistency and yield, and enhances operational safety in carcass processing environments.

The present invention relates to systems and methods for automated processing of animal carcasses, and more particularly to a cutting apparatus employing multiple independently-operated cutting tools for improved efficiency, precision, and yield in meat processing operations.

## Technical Summary

### Overview

The disclosed system comprises a multi-tool cutting apparatus configured to process animal carcasses through the coordinated yet independent operation of a plurality of cutting tools. Unlike conventional single-tool or fixed-sequence cutting systems, the present invention enables each cutting tool to operate autonomously, allowing simultaneous or sequential cutting operations at different anatomical locations.

### Key Components

The system may include:

1. **A support structure** configured to receive and secure an animal carcass in a predetermined orientation.

2. **A plurality of cutting tools**, each independently actuated and capable of performing distinct cutting operations. These may include reciprocating blades, rotary cutters, water-jet cutters, or laser cutting elements.

3. **Individual control modules** associated with each cutting tool, enabling independent adjustment of:
   - Cutting depth
   - Cutting angle and trajectory
   - Cutting speed
   - Actuation timing

4. **A sensing subsystem** (optional) that may include imaging devices, position sensors, or force feedback mechanisms to determine carcass dimensions, anatomical features, or tool position.

5. **A central control system** coordinating the independent tools while maintaining collision avoidance and process optimization.

- Determining cutting parameters for each tool (either through preset profiles or real-time sensing)
- Independently actuating the plurality of cutting tools to perform cutting operations
- Coordinating tool movements to prevent interference while maximizing throughput

### Advantages

The independent operation of multiple cutting tools may provide:
- Increased processing throughput through parallel operations
- Enhanced precision and consistency of cuts
- Improved yield through optimized cutting paths
- Flexibility to accommodate varying carcass sizes and types
- Reduced labor requirements

# ABSTRACT

An automated carcass butchering apparatus for processing animal carcasses includes a support frame having a plurality of independently actuated cutting assemblies mounted thereon. Each cutting assembly comprises a cutting tool coupled to an extendable actuator mechanism configured to transition between a retracted configuration and an extended configuration. In the retracted configuration, the cutting tools are positioned away from the carcass to permit loading, positioning, and removal of the carcass without interference. In the extended configuration, the cutting tools advance toward the carcass to perform cutting, sectioning, or deboning operations at predetermined anatomical locations.

The apparatus further includes a control system operatively connected to each cutting assembly, enabling independent movement of each cutting tool along one or more axes relative to the support frame and relative to the other cutting tools. This independent actuation permits simultaneous or sequential cutting operations to be performed at multiple locations along the carcass, accommodating variations in carcass size, shape, and orientation. Sensors may be provided to detect carcass dimensions and positioning, whereby the control system adjusts the extension depth, cutting path, and timing of each cutting tool accordingly.

The independent movement of the cutting tools, in combination with the selectable extended and retracted configurations, improves cutting precision, increases processing throughput, reduces product waste, and enhances operator safety by minimizing the need for manual intervention during the butchering process.
